sections.name: SystemsView (part 1)
sections.title: Overall completion and page header
sections.what: Adds up all steps across all routines to get a daily percent, then shows the page heading, a short explanation, the percent and the Reset Today button.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single number shows the day's overall progress.
sections.watch_out: Each step counts equally, so a long routine affects the percent more than a short one.

sections.name: SystemsView (part 2)
sections.title: Friction rule cards
sections.what: Completes the friction rules section with two more fixed cards: single-task anchoring and a daily rollover log. The rules are plain text in the file, not loaded from data.
sections.why: Likely reason: static advice shown beside the routines to explain the approach.
sections.watch_out: Changing these rules requires editing the file, since they are not stored anywhere else.

summary: The Systems page: a summary of today's routine completion, the routine cards, and a fixed set of friction rules.
purpose: Shows the user's daily routines and the rules that make habits easier to start.
why: Likely reason: combines progress and guidance on one page to keep routines running.
how: Adds up all items across all routines to get an overall percent. Shows a banner with that percent and a Reset Today button. Draws one card per routine. Ends with a set of fixed text cards describing friction rules.
inputs: The routines list and the reset action, both from the store.
outputs: The on-screen page. The reset button asks the store to reset today's routines.
risks: The overall percent counts every item equally, so longer routines carry more weight. The reset button has no confirmation. The friction rules are fixed text that cannot be edited in the app.
debug: If the percent looks wrong, check the completion flags on each routine item. If cards do not appear, check the routines list. If reset does nothing, check the reset function in the store.
